name: Chin-Up
summary: A bodyweight vertical pulling exercise using a supinated grip that targets the latissimus dorsi and elbow flexors.

setup: Grip the pull-up bar with a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing toward you and hands roughly shoulder-width apart.
Hang with fully extended arms and legs clear of the floor, engaging your core and pulling your shoulder blades slightly down to set an active hang.
steps: Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades while driving your elbows down and back toward your ribs.
Pull smoothly upward until your chin clears the height of the bar.
Pause briefly at the top without straining or craning your neck.
Lower yourself under control back down to a full active hang.
instructions.breathing: Exhale forcefully as you pull your body upward; inhale smoothly as you lower down under control.
cues: Drive your elbows into your back pockets.
Chest to the bar, not chin reaching over.
Stay tight through your midsection to prevent swinging.

common_faults.fault: Kicking the legs or swinging the torso to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to maintain a hollow-body position throughout the set.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the bottom range of motion short and failing to reach a full hang.
common_faults.correction: Lower completely until your elbows are fully extended before beginning the next repetition.

common_faults.fault: Reaching upward with the chin rather than pulling the chest to the bar.
common_faults.correction: Keep your neck neutral and focus on pulling your upper chest toward the bar.

precautions: Ensure the pull-up bar is securely mounted and rated for full body weight before hanging.
Step down safely rather than dropping from the top if fatigued.
